author: claude
desc: Measure the real limit on an m1n1-decoded xz initramfs. MEASURED SO FAR: expanded initramfs of 13.1, 50.8, 60.5 and 97.3 MiB all decode and boot; 278.9 MiB fails with m1n1 printing 'XZ decode failed', no 'FDT: initrd at' line, and the kernel therefore booting with an empty rootfs (rdinit=/sbin/init -> -2, then 'VFS: Cannot open root device' and reboot). The true limit lies in (97.3, 278.9] MiB. RULED OUT already, by inspection not assumption: XZ block-header size metadata (byte 13 flags are 0x0000 on every member, working and failing alike, so minilzlib's documented 'size metadata indicator' restriction is not it) and dictionary/filter differences (xz -lvv reports identical 1 stream / 1 block / CRC32 / 1 filter / 65 MiB for all). SUSPECT: m1n1's src/payload.c decodes into heapblock_alloc_aligned(0, KERNEL_ALIGN) — the uncommitted heap top — with dest_len = 1<<30, and heapblock_alloc_aligned performs NO bound check. TASK: bisect with intermediate rootfs sizes (try 128, 160, 192, 224 MiB expanded) OR, cheaper and offline first, build a host harness around m1n1's src/minilzlib (portable C, needs only stddef/stdint/stdbool/assert plus one ../utils.h include) and call XzDecode on the real members to find the threshold with no rig time. Then either fix m1n1's decompress path or set the verifier guard to the measured value. The verifier guard is currently 128 MiB — above every proven-good size, below the known-bad one — and MUST NOT be raised without a live boot proving the larger size decodes. Evidence: evidence/2026-07-26-t6040-initramfs-decode-limit.md.
result: 2026-07-27 HARNESS BUILT; the limit is NOT a simple size. scripts/t6040-minilzlib-harness.sh builds a host binary around m1n1's own src/minilzlib (byte-identical decoder, stub utils.h for printf) and t6040-minilzlib-harness.c mirrors payload.c decompress_xz (dest_len=1<<30). It reproduces the machine pass/fail EXACTLY on all objects (b0-nb2 13MiB, dwm-udev/hidpi 62MiB, kernel 50MiB all decode; fat 278MiB = 'XZ decode failed'), and since it reproduces on the host with a real 1 GiB buffer the failure is intrinsic to XzDecode, not target memory. So any initramfs can be cleared offline with zero rig time. KEY CORRECTION: the failure is CONTENT/LEVEL dependent, not a size threshold — 200 MiB of zeros decodes, 200 MiB real cpio at xz -6 decodes, 192 MiB real cpio at -9e decodes, but 278 MiB real cpio at -9e fails. Same uncompressed size passes or fails by compression level, pointing at LZMA2 chunk/range-decoder structure at -9e's 64 MiB dict, not byte count. Exact mechanism -> ticket 171. GUARD DECISION: no single expanded-size number is exactly right, so keep MAX_INITRAMFS_EXPANDED=128 MiB as a cheap backstop (every booted object is <=62 MiB; everything to 192 MiB -9e decodes) and treat lzharness as the authoritative pre-enroll check. FINISHING STEP: add --harness mode to t6040-raw-object-verify.py to shell out to lzharness. Evidence: evidence/2026-07-27-t6040-minilzlib-decode-limit-harness.md.
note: 2026-07-27 CORRECTION via 171: the limit is NOT content-dependent — it is a clean uncompressed-size cap at exactly 2^28 = 256 MiB, caused by the VLI_BYTES_MAX truncation bug (fix in patches/m1n1-minilzlib-vli-bytes-max.patch). My earlier 'content/level dependent' conclusion was premature; every passing case was <256 MiB and the failing case was >256 MiB. The 128 MiB verifier guard stays (well below 256 MiB); the harness is the authoritative check.
